definition: Estimating the number of objects in an image — crowd counting, cell counting — typically via density-map regression.
details: Estimating the number of objects in an image — crowd counting, cell counting — typically via density-map regression.

explainer.lead: Object counting estimates how many objects are in an image, as in crowd or cell counting. It matters where counting one by one is impractical, so systems often regress a density map instead.

tiers.eli5: Instead of pointing at each person in a crowd, it paints a heat map of where people are and adds up the heat to get a number.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train a network to output a density map and sum it for the count; a common pitfall is that dense, overlapping scenes make point-by-point detection unreliable.
tiers.paperLevel: A model maps an image to a density map whose integral over the image estimates the object count; accuracy depends on the density estimate, so severe overlap and perspective variation are known limits.

explainer.example: A density map over a stadium photo is summed to output an estimated attendance figure.

usedIn.name: Crowd monitoring
usedIn.detail: estimating crowd size in public spaces
